findings.condition: The saved component values give a discharge time constant tau = R1*C1 = 100 kOhm * 100 nF = 10 ms. The requirement (inputs/requirements.txt) demands /OUT <= 0.01 V at t = 5 ms after /IN is grounded with C1 pre-charged to 1 V and no external load.

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch (R1 Value "100k" at symbol uuid c5c38e1a-7593-5c99-b971-2f9d2e7bef78; C1 Value "100n" at symbol uuid 1dcaf7b4-dc79-5865-a3a4-db0c3eaad5d8)
findings.mechanism: With /IN grounded, C1's only discharge path is through R1 (netlist: R1 bridges /IN-/OUT, C1 bridges /OUT-GND; no other load). V(/OUT, 5 ms) = 1 V * exp(-5 ms / 10 ms) = 0.6065 V, exceeding the 0.01 V limit by a factor of ~60.7. The saved values would first reach 0.01 V at ~46 ms. Meeting the spec with C1 = 100n requires tau <= 5 ms / ln(100) = 1.086 ms, i.e. R1 <= ~10.86 kOhm (or equivalently a proportionally smaller C1). Both analytic calculation and an ngspice transient (vout_at_5ms = 6.065306e-01 V) agree.
findings.reasoning: This is the single stated functional acceptance criterion of the exercise, and the saved values miss it by ~60x, so the design as saved cannot pass regardless of layout quality. ERC, DRC, parity and connectivity all pass (confirmed by my independent re-runs), demonstrating that the clean tool exits in the packet are not evidence of electrical compliance. The failure is deterministic from the saved values under the mandated ideal-component assumption, so it is a defect, blocking against the packet scope.

findings.mechanism: I verified the path is electrically continuous as saved: pcbnew ratsnest reports 0 unconnected items and both J1.3 and the via geometrically collide with the saved B.Cu filled polygon. However, the sole functional return current path of the fixture has a single-point dependency on one small via and on the zone fill state; a lost/voided via barrel or an unfilled zone would open the GND net, and the saved file is the only fill state evaluated (refill is out of scope).
findings.reasoning: No stated requirement is violated: the scope is ideal connectivity only, connectivity is verified good as saved, and DRC passes, so this cannot be called a defect and carries no ampacity/thermal claim (none may be inferred from geometry alone). It is recorded as an informational concern because the entire functional net's return depends on one via plus zone fill with no redundancy, which is the kind of saved-board assumption a downstream revision (e.g., zone edit without refill) could silently break.
findings.title: GND return between C1 and J1 depends on a single 0.3 mm-drill via and the saved B.Cu zone fill (verified continuous as saved)

limitations: Zone fill evaluated exactly as saved; the read-only candidate forbids a refill pass, so fill-after-refill behavior was not assessed

No tolerance, parasitic (ESR/leakage), thermal, or ampacity analysis performed: the stated scope mandates ideal passive components and forbids imposing unstated ratings; no current/thermal requirement exists to evaluate against
Connector J1 mating/external-harness behavior (how /IN is grounded at t=0) is outside the board and was assumed ideal per the scenario
No manufacturing-output (gerber) generation or assembly review performed; not requested by the packet criteria
